decision: Persist the worker-side next request counter with atomic reserve-before-sign semantics

evaluatedApproaches.name: atomic-local-counter-file
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: restart-safe and unique across concurrent local worker processes sharing the state file
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: counter is durably reserved before a signed request is emitted, so crashes may create harmless gaps but cannot reuse an accepted counter
evaluatedApproaches.latency: one lock plus small atomic file rewrite per request
evaluatedApproaches.resourceUse: constant-size state and no request history
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: low-medium; workers must use PersistentWorkerSigner rather than choosing counters manually
evaluatedApproaches.qa: tests cover restart continuity, 64 concurrent reservations across 8 instances, signer restart, and restrictive POSIX permissions

evaluatedApproaches.name: memory-only-counter
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: fails after worker restart because the counter can regress to one
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: insufficient for coordinator durable replay fencing
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: low implementation cost but unsafe restart behavior

evaluatedApproaches.name: timestamp-derived-counter
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: clock rollback and same-tick concurrency can regress or collide
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: depends on wall-clock discipline across VM suspension/resume
evaluatedApproaches.regressionRisk: high correctness risk under Qubes pause/resume

evaluatedApproaches.name: coordinator-issued-counter-blocks
evaluatedApproaches.correctness: strong long-term option and amortizes persistence/network cost
evaluatedApproaches.robustness: requires a finalized authenticated Qubes transport and durable session semantics
evaluatedApproaches.latency: potentially best at scale when counters are reserved in blocks

whyItWon: It closes the immediate worker-restart replay gap with minimal code and constant state while matching the coordinator's existing monotonic-counter contract. Reserve-before-sign makes crash gaps safe and avoids counter reuse.
knownFailuresAndLessons: A lost or rolled-back worker state file causes safe coordinator rejection; re-enrollment needs an explicit operator-controlled counter reset/resynchronization protocol.
The state file is not a secret, but integrity matters; Qubes deployment should place it in worker-private persistent storage and prevent untrusted rollback.
Atomic rename and mkdir locking are LAB assumptions for one filesystem, not a cross-VM distributed primitive.
Per-request disk writes will become a throughput bottleneck; coordinator-issued counter blocks are the likely scale-up path after transport is fixed.
The counter does not provide confidentiality or transport authentication; those remain separate Qubes transport requirements.
